security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation-only, but several examples ask users to run shell commands against local databases and network services. Most static findings are Markdown or placeholder false positives; the real issues are unpinned CLI execution and a privileged firewall command.

remediation.issue: Unpinned package execution in CLI examples
remediation.suggestion: Replace agentdb@latest examples with pinned versions and tell users to inspect packages before running commands.

remediation.issue: Privileged firewall command in troubleshooting guidance
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit administrator approval warning and provide non-privileged diagnostic steps before sudo firewall changes.

remediation.issue: Database import, export, merge, and reindex examples handle local data stores
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to back up databases and protect exported files that may contain embeddings or memory records.

remediation.issue: Sample QUIC peers use private network addresses
remediation.suggestion: Label the IP addresses as placeholders and remind users to review network exposure before enabling QUIC sync.

content.value_statement: Advanced AgentDB projects need reliable patterns for sync, search, and database operations. This skill gives practical guidance for QUIC sync, hybrid search, sharding, and production tuning.
actual_capabilities: Explains AgentDB QUIC synchronization with ports, peers, batching, retries, and compression options.
Compares cosine, Euclidean, dot product, and custom distance metrics for vector search workloads.
Shows hybrid vector and metadata search patterns with filters, weights, and result diversification.
Describes multi-database separation, sharding by domain, and routing queries to the right adapter.
Covers production patterns for connection pooling, error handling, monitoring, import, export, and troubleshooting.
limitations: It does not install AgentDB or verify that the referenced package version supports every option.
Examples use placeholder peers and local database paths that must be changed for real deployments.
It assumes Node.js, AgentDB, and vector search fundamentals are already available.
It is not a complete security hardening guide for exposed QUIC services or database backups.

use_cases.title: Plan Distributed Memory Sync
use_cases.description: Use the skill to design QUIC peer settings, sync intervals, retries, and deployment checks for AgentDB nodes.

use_cases.title: Tune Retrieval Quality
use_cases.description: Use the skill to choose distance metrics, combine metadata filters, and balance relevance with result diversity.

use_cases.title: Operate AgentDB Data Stores
use_cases.description: Use the skill to organize multiple databases, export backups, merge stores, rebuild indexes, and monitor latency.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Distance Metric
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a vector search feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain which AgentDB distance metric fits my workload. My data is [type], vectors are [normalized or raw], and speed needs are [goal].

prompt_templates.title: Design Hybrid Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an AgentDB hybrid search approach for [domain]. Include useful metadata filters, scoring weights, and diversity settings.

prompt_templates.title: Plan QUIC Sync
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan QUIC synchronization for [number] AgentDB nodes across [environment]. Include peer layout, ports, retry settings, and operational risks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my AgentDB production plan for [application]. Assess database separation, sharding, backup operations, monitoring, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: Choose a distance metric for semantic document search with normalized text embeddings.
output_examples.output: Use cosine similarity as the default. It focuses on direction, works well for normalized text vectors, and supports semantic similarity search.

output_examples.input: Plan database separation for knowledge, conversations, and code memories.
output: Use separate AgentDB files for each memory domain.
Route writes by domain before inserting patterns.
Monitor size, latency, and cache hit rate for each store.

output_examples.input: Troubleshoot QUIC synchronization that is not reaching peer nodes.
output_examples.output: Check UDP firewall rules, confirm peer names resolve, verify matching ports, and review QUIC logs before changing production settings.

best_practices: Use placeholder peer addresses until the deployment network plan is approved.
Pin package versions before running CLI examples in production environments.
Encrypt and access-control exported database backups that may contain embeddings or memory records.
anti_patterns: Do not run privileged firewall commands from examples without administrator approval.
Do not reuse sample private IP addresses in real peer configuration.
Do not merge or reindex production databases without a tested backup and rollback plan.

faq.question: Does this skill execute AgentDB commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that a user or agent may choose to run.

faq.question: What AgentDB topics does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers QUIC sync, distance metrics, hybrid search, multi-database patterns, MMR, monitoring, and CLI operations.

faq.question: Is it useful for beginners?
faq.answer: It is best for users who already understand Node.js, vectors, and basic AgentDB usage.

faq.question: Can it help with production deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It discusses pooling, retries, monitoring, database maintenance, and troubleshooting patterns.

faq.question: Does it include security hardening?
faq.answer: Only limited operational cautions are included. Users should add network, backup, and access-control reviews.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
